title: Evaluation Frameworks 101: Why Vibes Don't Scale
author: Jason D.
excerpt: If you can't measure it, you can't improve it. Here's how to build an evaluation framework that catches failures before production does.
content:
"It looks about right." "The output seems reasonable." "I think it's working."

These are the three most dangerous phrases in AI engineering. They're vibes. And vibes don't scale.

What Is an Evaluation Framework?

An evaluation framework is an automated system that tests your AI agent against known scenarios and measures its performance objectively. Think of it as a test suite for AI, but more sophisticated than unit tests.

A good evaluation framework includes:

  • Golden datasets — Curated input/output pairs that represent expected behavior
  • Edge case libraries — Known tricky scenarios that have caused failures
  • Regression tests — Ensure fixes don't break previously working scenarios
  • Performance benchmarks — Latency, throughput, and cost baselines
  • Confidence calibration — Is the agent's confidence score actually predictive?

Why Most Teams Skip This

Building evals isn't glamorous. It's not as exciting as training a new model or building a fancy UI. But it's the single most important investment you can make in an AI system.

Teams skip evaluation because:

  • It feels slow ("we need to ship")
  • It's hard to define "correct" for subjective tasks
  • There's no existing tooling in their stack
  • Leadership doesn't ask for it (until something breaks)

Building Your First Eval Suite

Start simple. You don't need a perfect eval suite on day one. Start with:

# eval_suite/
# Start with 50-100 test cases across these categories:

test_categories:
  happy_path: 30%       # Standard, expected inputs
  edge_cases: 30%       # Unusual but valid inputs  
  adversarial: 20%      # Deliberately tricky inputs
  regression: 20%       # Previously failed scenarios

Run this suite on every change. No exceptions. If a change improves accuracy on one category but degrades another, you'll catch it immediately.

Measuring What Matters

Don't just measure accuracy. Measure:

  • Accuracy by category — Where is the agent strong vs. weak?
  • Failure mode distribution — How does the agent fail? (Wrong answer vs. no answer vs. hallucination)
  • Confidence calibration — When the agent says it's 90% sure, is it right 90% of the time?
  • Latency distribution — p50, p95, p99 response times
  • Cost per evaluation — Track spend to prevent runaway costs

An evaluation framework isn't overhead. It's the foundation that makes everything else — iteration, deployment, monitoring — possible.

The Bottom Line

If you're running an AI agent in production without automated evaluations, you're flying blind. Build the eval suite first. Make it a non-negotiable part of your development process. Your future self will thank you.
